# Multi-Level Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This document is a companion to
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md). It
> expands the RFC's phase sequence into **independently committable and independently verifiable
> three-level tasks**.
>
> The phase sequence and acceptance gates defined in the main body of RFC-039 are the sole
> authority. This document is responsible only for decomposing the work to an executable granularity
> and registering conflicts that have not yet been adjudicated.

**Numbers left vacant (not reused)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`. None of the three
has had a corresponding entry since the WBS was established—the full history of this document has
zero matches for the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1` (this can be verified with
`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md`), and there are no
repository-wide references. `8.1` corresponds precisely to stage 1 of `05` (test revival and
completion): that stage has already been split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so P8's numbering is
aligned with its phase numbers (phase 0 → `8.0`, phase 2 → `8.2`, and so forth).

**Covered by this document**: task decomposition, dependencies, parallel groups, and binding of
acceptance criteria.

**Not covered by this document**: the design rationale for tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the rationale
for phase ordering (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: newly registered Level 2/Level 3 rows **must
contain two fields**—“**Owning phase**” (the P to which the task truly belongs, which may differ
from the containing section) and “**Blocks the main line**”; `pending scheduling` is no longer the
default state, and an unmarked task is treated as **not schedulable**. Numbers must be **unique
across the entire document** (tasks spanning tracks use the track number, such as `029g.x`, and must
not occupy an `N.x` number). **Checkoff/completion registration is based on “task ID + evidence
(gate values, run ID, issue number, file:line),” not a commit hash**—`pull --rebase` rewrites local
hashes, so a hard-coded hash inevitably becomes invalid (2026-10-13 example:
`94ad03ce4`→`631eb3e3c`). Look up commit hashes with `git log`.

## Current State: Gaps Discovered During Decomposition

When the “Implementation Points” from eight documents were consolidated into the master table,
**five hard gaps in the documentation system itself** were discovered. All have now been resolved:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Resolution                                                                                                                                               |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G1  | **P5 has no implementation steps whatsoever.** RFC-039 defines P5 (checker decomposition) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but not one of the seven documents describes how to perform the decomposition; the directory tree in `01-routing.md` contains a single mention of `annotations.rs`, the only mention in the entire batch                             | The P5 steps are supplied by this document (see below)                                                                                                   |
| G2  | **The three ownership claims for the `include!` refactor have zero implementations.** RFC-039 places it in P4; `02` claims it for itself; and `06` S7 also lists it. However, the change list in `02` (6 additions + 20 modifications) contains **no `semantic_tokens.rs`**                                                                                                 | The implementation steps are assigned to §P5 5.1 in this document (after P4 is complete); the references in RFC-039 and `06` have been redirected here   |
| G3  | **Three coexisting lists of CI scripts.** `RFC` lists four `scripts/ci/*.py`; `01` lists four scripts + one `cargo test`; `07` lists four other checks with entirely different names; and `04` also requires `check-synth-boundary.py`. After deduplication, there are **at least nine new scripts and no unified list**; `check-obligations.py` is owned by both P4 and P9 | See §P9 in this document for the unified list (11 scripts, each owned by exactly one phase); all other documents refer to this table                     |
| G4  | **Conflict over the life cycle of `precedence_inline.rs`.** `06` counts it among the “1005 lines that must be revived,” while B6 in the same document says it “must be deleted together with the `Precedence` enum”; `05` advocates deletion                                                                                                                                | **Revive in P1; delete with Pratt in P8** (decision registered as C1)—first restore CI coverage, then delete the file in 8.6 alongside the dead ladder   |
| G5  | **Conflicting descriptions of the L2 goal.** RFC-039 and this directory's index say “grammar-driven syntax,” but `05` self-assesses: “**we did not adopt true grammar-driven syntax (LALRPOP); we only implemented declarative table lookup**”                                                                                                                              | Resolved as **fully grammar-driven using LALRPOP** (`05` §Syntax: fully grammar-driven); the G7/G8 acceptance gates are executed against that commitment |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0  仓库维护机制与代码放置规程     08        ← 新增，先立规矩
P1  复活孤儿测试并修缺陷           06 §S1
P2  建立等价性判据基线             07 全部
P3  修正确性漏洞（最小方案）        02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4  阶段契约与统一 Driver          02
P5  checker 文件内拆分             02 + 本文补齐
P6  类型表示单一化                 03
P7  中间表示 SSA 化                04      } 可并行
P8  前端范式变更                   05      }
P9  防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单）     01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正             06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Rationale for adding P0**: the three prohibitions (no invention, no endless padding, and no
patching when a refactor is required) constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules must be
established before work begins; otherwise, when P1 revives tests, it will already be adding `mod`
declarations to `tests/mod.rs`—which is precisely what caused conflict G4.

> **Semantic-correction routing (D59, user adjudication on 2026-10-11)**: if this track or a later
> phase discovers a defect for which “the old behavior did not count as success”—**A silent failure
> / B silent mismatch / C undefined behavior and resource loss** (crash, stack overflow, or silently
> returning the wrong answer)—it **may be fixed along the way with the refactor**, but all four
> conditions are mandatory: ① red before green (the red criterion must exist first and must actually
> be red); ② do not change the externally observable behavior of programs that “previously compiled
> successfully and ran correctly” (they must not become failures, and existing diagnostic
> codes/text/exit codes must not be removed or modified); ③ register in the same commit (the row
> identifies the defect type + a revision note for that phase + a required “Defect Type” line in the
> PR block); ④ regenerate the baseline in the same commit + manually review the diff. **The three
> categories D user-visible semantics / E external contract tables / F RFC-level design changes must
> still receive user adjudication first.** See
> [07 §Semantic-Correction Routing Criteria](07-equivalence-oracle.md) for the expanded criteria and
> A–F whitelist; **“default super-refactor + post-hoc registration” is not accepted** (the rationale
> is in RFC-039 D59: without a zero-red criterion, repairs cannot be distinguished from regressions,
> and this conflicts with both “there is no C5′” and “no relaxation of any kind”).

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted on 2026-10-02;
implementation has not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This
track is not a design item of the refactor itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced
by an ordering constraint**; it is separate from P10 S5 “reduce the visibility of `pub` items”
(narrowing Rust's `pub(crate)`).

**Why it must be completed before P4 as a whole**: 029g's deletion surface overlaps the rewrite
surfaces of all four refactor phases; reversing the order means redoing the same deletions and
baseline updates over the new grammar / new checker layout / new SSA IR.

**Acceptance (behavior changes; red criterion first)**:

1. **Red before green**: each of the two behavior changes must have its red criterion in place
   before code changes—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② an unreferenced
   top-level binding in the Lib/Script role newly reports W1001 (pub items were previously always
   exempt).
2. **Test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` case in
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs` and the `is_pub` fixtures, equivalent new cases must
   replace them.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (new parse error + new W1001) ⇒ update
   the corpus-differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG in the
   same commit; IR snapshots are expected to have zero diff, and any difference requires an
   explanation.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` all pass.

**Ordering**: it overlaps 3.4 in files (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) ⇒ the two must be serial and
cannot run in parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g track does not
depend on 3.4; the implementer chooses which to start first based on the context at hand.

> adjudication filing” and does not mention this track. History is not rewritten; following the
> existing convention (the `d5b18390` precedent, see the P2 landing note), it is registered in place
> as evidence for later bisecting.

|                             | 5.2.2 Consolidate the refinement entry point as “`&self` + return diagnostics,” **without leaving the impl**: `collect_refined_binding_checks` (now `checker/refinement.rs`, `pub(super)`) no longer uses `&mut self` to write to the implicit error channel; the diagnostic set is returned and propagated upward, with the sole write location in the sole caller `check_module_impl` (`checker.rs`, symbol location). **Rationale for remaining in the impl**: this family's field surface contains only `self.env` (so leaving the impl is technically possible), but converting both the entry point and the walk to free functions would move these call sites: `resolve_type_annotation` has 8 production locations (6 annotation paths + `refined_walk_stmt` + `collect_refined_var_names_in_stmt`), `collect_param_refinements` has 2 production locations + 1 test, and would create a reverse dependency from the “retention surface (signature collection)” to refinement—the opposite of this step's intent to eliminate coupling | 5.2.1         | C1 zero-diff; four **symbol criteria**: ① the signature contains no `&mut self`; ② the function body contains zero `env.errors`; ③ the diagnostic returned by the entry point is written in exactly one location in the caller; ④ the entry point still has exactly 1 location |
| 5.3 Extract `annotations`   | 5.3.1 Move out the 10-item annotation-validation family (now one file, `checker/annotations.rs`; `check_annotation_type_names` is the `pub(super)` entry point, the other 9 items are private to the family, and `is_predicate_head` is a family-local free function)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | 5.2.2         | C1 zero-diff                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|                             | 5.3.2 **Keep `collect_used_in_type` (`pub(crate)`) as `pub(crate)` under the `checker` module path**: it is a **shared-surface** function (consumed by both `collect_function_signature` and `inference/statements.rs:16`), and 5.3.1 **did not migrate it** as measured ⇒ the “zero caller changes” criterion **was already satisfied**, so **do not add** a new `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export. **Constraint retained**: if it is moved with the family in the future (into annotations or another later batch), `checker.rs` must add a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that this import remains unchanged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | 5.3.1         | **Zero caller changes** is this step's hard acceptance criterion: `git diff src/frontend/core/typecheck/inference/statements.rs` is empty                                                                                                                                      |

**Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is moved with the annotation family in the future, **then** `checker.rs` must
add a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that this import remains unchanged; as measured,
5.3 did **not** move it, so this batch added no re-export (the criterion was already satisfied).

**Only decompose confirmed large blocks.** Do not decompose modules of only 200–400 lines—this adds
navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and provides zero decoupling benefit. The remaining submodules
(signatures / type_defs / imports) are deferred until the file grows back to 1,500 lines.

after t4, **214/218** (4 skipped: `deep_recursion_within_limit` / `explicit_termination_measure` / `measure_decreasing` / `stack_overflow_e6004`). “`corpus-parity.jsonl:133` records diagnostics: [] / exit: 0” and the snapshot path's E3006 do not constitute “the two criteria reaching opposite conclusions about the same file”—the corpus baseline is produced by the CLI/driver, and the driver has long injected the probe, so the snapshot criterion itself supplied the wrong AST. **Both original errors were corrected**: ① it was not “pre-existing / present since 2026-10-12”; ② the pending adjudication option “fix ir_gen's E3006 path” was **withdrawn**—ir_gen is correct to report the error; the error was that the criterion supplied it with the wrong AST. **Fix** (change only the criterion, with zero product-code changes): change the entry point to `parse_with_probe(&tokens, &SemanticProbe)` (the same as the driver); replace the relaxed `assert!(compared > 200)` lower bound with a **reconciliation assertion**—if `reaches_ir_generation` is true but no normalized text is available, **fail and name each case**, and assert `compared == reachable`; the update process must likewise treat “skipped” as red (otherwise stale snapshots are neither compared nor updated). After the fix, **218/218**, and `measure_decreasing.snap` also converges to the narrowed-carrier form (`type_decl []`—that type body contains only const-bound expressions and no data fields), with the snapshot surface's residual spans reduced to zero. Measured: restoring bare `parse()` makes the new assertion fail and list the 4 files above (coverage 214/218) |

**Hard acceptance** (**criterion revised on 2026-10-27, inheriting adjudication ② from
2026-10-26**): `git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be **empty in every
round of 6.1–6.7**. **Direct-drive test files** under `tests/` (tests that drive the changed code,
such as `tests/formatter_integration.rs`) may be modified **when mechanically required by the
change**, but each change must be registered with **file / line count / rationale**; **tests must
not be deleted and assertions must not be weakened**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavior-fix**
batch (new diagnostic code + baseline update), does not satisfy this hard acceptance criterion, and
runs as a separate round with separate adjudication.

> **Revision relationship**: the original criterion (2026-10-26 adjudication ②) read
> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, treating all of `tests/` as requiring zero differences; the
> revised criterion **changes direct-drive test files from “zero difference” to “may be changed but
> must register file / line count / rationale,”** while **the zero-difference requirement for the
> corpus layer (`tests/yaoxiang`), baseline layer (`tests/baselines`), and standard library
> (`src/std/`) remains unchanged**. First application = 6.1.2: only `tests/formatter_integration.rs`
> changed by **3 lines** (2 `assert_format_eq` instances, `i64`→`Int64`, plus 1 comment line), with
> the rationale = the expected type name in the assertion must be synchronized with the changed
> spelling; no tests were deleted and no assertions were weakened. See 09a “P6 6.1 Name
> Normalization Closure” for details.

non-equivalence, the problem must be solved before switching traffic in 8.5, rather than being
masked after the switch by C5′. If any of the approximately 89 BP references are missed during 8.6's
migration, associativity will **silently change** (no error, only a different parse result).

## Implementation Points: Dependencies and Parallelism

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 emergency stop-loss path (user adjudication on 2026-10-05)**: P3's prerequisites are narrowed
> to **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (the multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The rest of P2 (2.1
> IR verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential and performance baseline) can proceed in
> parallel with P3. Stopping the bleed for a correctness defect is not blocked by
> criterion-infrastructure work; but **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified Driver needs
> all three layers of criteria in place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every action in P1 (1.2.x is precisely where `mod` declarations are added to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| P1 → P2                   | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | The vulnerability criteria must be **written in red first** (2.4.1/2.4.3) + the multi-file corpus layer (2.3.2) must exist so that the red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                  |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; the reverse order would cause bugs to become institutionalized as “established behavior” in the stage table                                                                                                                                                                |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g (#399)'s deletion surface covers the rewrite targets of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 respectively (the list is in this document's §P3.5)—the reverse order means redoing the same deletions over the new grammar, new checker layout, and new IR (D56)                                         |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` refactor and checker decomposition touch the same file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separated; otherwise regressions cannot be located by bisection                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | If type representations do not converge first, the new IR will grow into a third representation; P7's gate in the #529 implementation line is 6.9.1–6.9.4, and 6.9.5 does not block it, but P7 may consume only quantifier-derived views and the defeq interface, and must not create a parallel ledger |
| P7/P8 → P9                | The 9.5 snapshot baseline and the 9.3 `pub(crate)` leak count reach their final forms only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

### Parallelizable Groups

| Group                                    | Members                                                                            | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **A (the only group authorized by RFC)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                            | Disjoint file sets: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                          |
| B                                        | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                      | Each independently adds a `mod`; revert file by file                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| C                                        | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                    | The three layers of criteria are independent                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| D                                        | 4.4 (proof-layer closure) ∥ the entire P6 line                                     | `02` explicitly states under S5 that it “should proceed independently of S1-S4”                                                                                                                                                                        |
| E                                        | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                              | All are independent after 4.1 is complete                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| F                                        | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced in P0 can be developed in parallel) | The 9.5 snapshot baseline must be taken last                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| G                                        | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                       | Disjoint file sets (verified on 2026-10-05: S3 touches `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 touches `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 touches two `pub` locations in `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; no pair overlaps) |

**Cannot run in parallel (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (B6/E5 in
the same batch of files); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (now unified into P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` /
`environment.rs` are the same files—the external track's pub-deletion batch and the silent-channel
fixes must be serial).

**New internal documentation constraint**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial;
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial, and 7b's `Phi` arm must precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is a separate phase rather than part of P9**—gates are “post-hoc checks,” while rules are
  “pre-hoc judgment.” P9's scripts cannot prevent “patching when a refactor is required”; only
  D0–D4's review checklist can.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative list of CI scripts**—the original gap G3's three coexisting lists
  made closure impossible. This table merges them, assigns each of the 11 scripts to exactly one
  phase, and makes report-only status and conversion timing explicitly traceable.
- **P3.5 incorporates RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to execute after the
  refactor”**—its deletion surface overlaps the rewrite surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039 D56).
  Deferring it until after the refactor means redoing the same deletions over the new grammar, new
  checker layout, and new IR; this is the same lesson as incorporating `2315`/`2341` in 7e and the
  RFC status corrections into S4.
- **P5's steps are supplied by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding checker decomposition would exceed the rollback granularity.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero caller changes” as hard acceptance**—decomposition must be independently
  revertible.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fix exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it only says “the fixed defects must
  not be rolled back,” and lacks a requirement to record “what was fixed.” **Execution convention**:
  every 1.3.x fix's commit message must reference the fixed test name and defect description, as
  evidence for later bisecting.
- ~~**7b.1's granularity is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b as two
  exclusive commits per DoD 6.
- **8.2.1's granularity is too coarse**—approximately 89 references are renamed, and a missed edit
  **silently changes associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding Level 3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 lands as 7e.1,
  D20 lands as 4.5.1/4.5.2; the D32/D34 opcode reclamation is merged into 7e.1, and the deletion
  action remains in P10 S6.
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally assigned to “independent issues”**~~
  **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated as 7e.2 / 7e.3. The exception table (throw/try) is core
  language semantics and must not be left as an unimplemented legacy.
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: merged into
  P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: merged into the
  generation-time gate task in P10 S6.

| C3          | Conflict between C6 category definition and S1 classification                  | **S1 is classified under C6** (revival does not require an equivalence criterion, only regression tests); the C6 definition is expanded to “pure deletion or pure revival” |
| C4          | `test_release_plan_spans_consumed` whitelist                                   | **No whitelist**; the set difference must be empty; if it cannot be empty, the `ReleasePlan` contract is defective → change it to `PlanId` (D20/D41)                       |
| C5          | Internal differences between the two `Aggregation` functions were not verified | **P4's 4.2.7 lists this as a mandatory verification item**; confirm line by line during implementation                                                                     |
| C6          | The wasm playground fix requires P4's `ProgramKind`                            | **The wasm-path defect fix is merged into 4.2.8**; P3 handles only the three native entry points                                                                           |
| C7          | Ownership of `method_def_ordinals`                                             | **Assigned to 04** (P7 batch c), see D21                                                                                                                                   |
| C8          | `upvalue_count` correction and the `.42` version number                        | **Fix + raise `VERSION` from 4 to 5** (the format header already has `MAGIC` + `VERSION` fields, `codegen/bytecode.rs:14-16`), see D17                                     |
